Quality.label: Fog quality
Quality.help: How fine the volumetric fog is. Higher looks better and asks more of the graphics card.

Temporal.label: Smoothing over time
Temporal.help: Blends each frame with the previous ones, for a fog without grain. 0 = off.

Density.label: Fog density
Density.help: How much fog there is everywhere in the world. 1 = the amount each zone was made with.

Haze.label: Distance haze
Haze.help: Haze in the distance, where the game has no Classic fog of its own.

GroundFog.label: Ground mist
GroundFog.help: Low mist near the ground, where the game has no Classic fog of its own.

FarFog.label: Distance fog
FarFog.help: The distance fog that replaces the game's own.

DataMode.label: Classic fog layers
DataMode.help: Uses World of Warcraft Classic's fog layers where they exist. Off: computed layers everywhere.

Exposure.help: Brightness of the computed fog layers, where the game has no Classic data.

ColorSpace.help: Computes light as the later game clients do, with soft highlights. Several colour settings need it. Off: the classic (gamma) way.

ShaftRange.label: Shaft range
ShaftRange.help: How far from the camera shafts are traced. Lower is lighter on the graphics card.

ShaftMemory.label: Shaft memory
ShaftMemory.help: Trees and buildings already seen keep shading the shafts once off screen: turning the camera does not change the shafts, and the gaps between leaves stay open. Off: only what is on screen.

LampFog.help: Torches, candles, braziers and lanterns placed in the world glow in the air, more in rain, snow or sand; by day as much as “Lamps by day” allows; none in the ghost world. 0 = off.

LampCount.help: How many lamps in view glow and light things, brightest first. Fewer is lighter on the graphics card. Lamps reach 800 yd.

EffectLight.help: Glowing spells, projectiles, enchants and other bright effects light the ground, walls and characters around them in their own colour, up to 6 at a time. In rain or snow only coloured glows count. 0 = off.

ObjectLamps.label: Fires placed by the server
ObjectLamps.help: Campfires, braziers, candles and torches the server places (cooking fires, camps, festival braziers) light and glow like the lamps of the world, where they stand. Off: they only give spell light.

CorpseLight.help: Corpses you can loot give a small golden twinkle of light, the nearest 4 within 40 yd. By day as much as “Lamps by day” allows; none in the ghost world. 0 = off.

Relief.label: Ground relief
Relief.help: Paved roads, tiles, stones and rock on the ground get depth: they shift with the view, catch the light on their sunlit side and shade themselves. Needs the game's exterior shadows at quality 3 to 5.

ReliefModels.label: Relief on models
ReliefModels.help: Trees, creatures, characters, armour and props get relief too. It is made while you play, the first time each texture shows.

ReliefDepth.label: Relief depth
ReliefDepth.help: How deep the relief is at its deepest, for stone and paving; each texture type gets its share of it (below).

WaterBump.label: Ripples
WaterBump.help: Fine ripples drift with the wind over the waves and bend the reflections. 0 = off.

WaterFoam.label: Foam
WaterFoam.help: Foam where the water is shallow along the shores, drifting with the wind. 0 = off.

TerrainMaterials.label: Ground materials
TerrainMaterials.help: Tells the ground's material from its texture: grass, soil, stone, sand, snow, ice, wood or lava. Off: each surface is judged by its colour. Needs the game's exterior shadows at quality 3 or more.

LiquidDepth.label: Water depth
LiquidDepth.help: Water surfaces take the fog of their own distance. The water's reflections and effects need it.

FarClipMax.help: The game caps the view on the continents at 791 yd; Lumenveil allows up to 1583 yd. Further looks better and asks much more of the PC. Turning it on when it was off at the game's start needs a restart of the game.

PerfLog.label: Performance log
PerfLog.help: Writes to the log every 60 seconds how long each part of the effect takes. Useful to report a slowdown.

Enable.help: Off: the game looks as it does without Lumenveil, which stays installed. Takes effect at the next start of the game.

EngineHooks.label: Access to the game's engine
EngineHooks.help: What gives the lamps, water, relief, shadows and longer view distance. Off: the fog only. Takes effect at the next start of the game.

ZoneDensity.help: Fog density of particular zones: the zone's number and a multiplier of the density, comma-separated (148:0.5,490:0.7). Easier from the game: the in-game settings window sets the zone you stand in.

DryZones.help: The zones that count as dry (dust haze, scattered clouds), by zone number, comma-separated.

GreenZones.help: The zones that count as green (humid haze, more clouds), by zone number, comma-separated.

PlainGame.label: Original game
PlainGame.help: On: the game shows without Lumenveil, as the compare key shows it, at once and at every start. Off: Lumenveil shows.
